name: MLB-RP36 reliever shadow addendum
summary: Reliever shadow addendum consumed by MLB-M0. MLB-RP36 owns the first-up reliever cluster artifact, bullpen path context, availability/bridge risk notes, and a May 31 run envelope with source/input/output locks.
keyImprovements: Separates the relief stack from the parent MLB model without promoting it to a competing model.
Replaces the old experiment label with the canonical MLB-RP36 cartridge name.
Documents the current source chain before moving any relief code.
Tightens the role boundary: MLB-RP36 can downgrade side/total/prop confidence through bridge risk, but cannot graduate a standalone pick from first-up reliever guesses.
Adds a dated run envelope so relief addendum source, lightweight warehouse inputs, outputs, and exact snapshot reproduction can be verified independently from MLB-M0.

keyMetrics.label: Latest audited exact first-up
keyMetrics.details: May 30 target-date shadow check, 20 team-side games graded.

keyMetrics.label: First locked run
keyMetrics.details: May 31, 2026 is the first reproducible RP36 run envelope; May 30 remains legacy context because the current warehouse no longer regenerates it exactly.

notes: MLB-RP36 should inform sides, totals, props, and late-game risk; it should not produce final board picks alone.
May 31 is the first behavior-preserving run-lock target. May 30 is useful legacy context, but not an exact reproducible RP36 run from the current warehouse.
The exporter still emits `E36 shadow` in payload metadata for historical continuity; the cartridge identity is MLB-RP36.
Use top-2/top-3 cluster confidence as context before exact first-up identity; exact first-up is too noisy at the current audit rate.
knownLimitations: Run locks are file-based for now and are not yet written into shared model-run DB tables.
No settlement table exists for first-up reliever predictions yet.
Current artifacts are useful but not standalone betting signals.
